article.name: Emulo
article.summary: Emulo mines user-authored coding-agent session logs into dated, quote-backed Markdown instruction profiles. It provides a local extractor and a plugin/bootstrap workflow with report validation and versioned profile activation. Retrieval loads whole domain profiles rather than performing ranked memory search; runtime quality and efficiency were not measured.

who_what.text: The official README describes Emulo as a local Python tool and agent integration that mines supported coding-agent logs into personal instruction profiles. It names Ohad Krispin as maintainer. The two documented profile-generation paths are a manual chunk export and an agent plugin/bootstrap flow.

architecture.text: The Python extractor selects user-authored messages from supported source formats, filters injected content and pasted logs, redacts common sensitive values, deduplicates long repeated messages, and writes session/date-labeled text. Redaction is documented as best-effort.

The manual path writes corpus chunks, stats, and RUN_ME.md for a separate agent to author a profile. The plugin path stages segments, reports, reductions, and validated domain profiles under a local Emulo home, then activates a versioned profile through a manifest-checked current pointer.

behavior.text: Writes begin with local extraction of recognized human-authored turns, filtering and redaction. The manual flow leaves profile authoring to the agent; the plugin flow documents preflight planning, explicit plan approval before model work, validated worker reports, reduction, and activation. No mining run was performed in this review.

A manual Markdown profile can be reviewed/edited and installed to a supported host. Plugin-managed active files are hash-checked against their manifest, so direct edits are refused by loaders; the documented update path is to mine again. Documentation describes deleting emulo-out or the complete local ~/.emulo store. No per-rule delete API, tombstone, or remote deletion protocol was found.

Retrieval loads whole instruction files: the work profile and optionally the design, writing, or video domain profile. The MCP tool load_emulo_profile returns selected profile text. There is no source-inspected relevance-ranked retrieval index or query-based memory search.

Data is organized by one user's local home/configured EMULO_HOME and by profile domain. I found no tenant, project, or session authorization boundary on profile reads; local paths and domain selection do not themselves establish access control.

Dated quotes and session identifiers provide traceability to captured messages. The plugin workflow documents checks for quote presence, distinct-session support, contradictions, and generic rules; standalone verify searches quoted spans in the corpus and flags single-session support. These checks do not establish that a rule is true, current, or useful.

Content hashes and caches support reuse of unchanged segment/report work; README describes identical plugin updates as planning zero additional Emulo mining calls. Planned source tokens and worker/reducer counts are not actual provider billing. The usage report prints counts and message examples; no operational telemetry or performance data was gathered.

metrics.evidence: Profile loading was inspected; no answerability, ranking, or abstention workload was run.
Regeneration is documented, but no per-rule correction or stale-value probes were run.
Local removal instructions were inspected; no residual-read or secure-erasure probe was run.
Local path and domain organization were inspected; no cross-user or cross-project isolation workload was run.
Quote/session lineage and validation source were inspected; no adjudicated output-claim support or citation coverage was scored.
No token, provider billing, or storage measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a source review at the verified main head. Emulo, its tests, and benchmarks were not run.

Rule quality, retrieval usefulness, malformed/adversarial log robustness, hosted-model retention, tenant safety, secure deletion, latency, actual provider cost, and scaling remain unknown from this review.

benchmark.note: No Emulo runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Project metric definitions and comparison fixtures are not Emulo results.
